_note: Compensation: the definition (CW6 ¶694), the self-regulating psyche (CW8 ¶159, ¶132, CW7 ¶274), the dream's corrective work (CW7 ¶170, CW18 ¶1391), the refusal to call it opposition (CW5 ¶98, CW16 ¶12), the ordering factor (CW11 ¶447, CW3 ¶582), and Van Eenwyk where the concept names a dynamical system. Quotations are placed by the corpus; nothing is typed.
line: The psyche's self-regulation: what consciousness leaves out returns from the unconscious, not as an enemy but as an adjustment — and the dream is where this work is done.

sections.title: The definition
sections.line: Jung widens the word past Adler: compensation is not the patching of inferiority feelings but the psyche's inherent self-regulation.

quotes.quote: Whereas Adler restricts his concept of compensation to the balancing of inferiority feelings, I conceive it as functional adjustment in general, an inherent self-regulation of the psychic apparatus.

sections.title: The self-regulating psyche
sections.line: The model is the body's: a system that answers imbalance with counteraction, and whose equilibrium depends on the other side being spoken.

quotes.quote: Since the psyche is a self-regulating system, just as the body is, the regulating counteraction will always develop in the unconscious
the unconscious behaves in a compensatory or complementary manner towards the conscious
conscious and unconscious are not necessarily in opposition to one another, but complement one another to form a totality, which is the self

sections.title: The dream's other side
sections.line: In practice, most dreams do this work: they stress what the waking attitude left out.

quotes.quote: in my experience the vast majority of dreams are compensatory.11 They always stress the other side in order to maintain the psychic equilibrium.
As a rule the meaning of a dream is compensatory to the conscious attitude, i.e., it adds to the latter what was lacking in it.

sections.title: Not opposition
sections.line: The word is chosen against 'contrary': the complement acts purposively, and cannot be predicted mechanically.

quotes.quote: not merely mechanical or complementary, but rather compensatory
the conscious attitude of the neurotic is unnaturally onesided and must be balanced by complementary or compensatory contents deriving from the unconscious

sections.title: The ordering factor
sections.line: What arrives as compensation is often a whole figure, not a patch: the ordering symbols — mandala, quaternity — surface exactly when orientation is lost.

quotes.quote: a compensatory ordering factor which is independent of the ego and whose nature transcends consciousness
Mandala symbols appear very frequently in moments of psychic disorientation as compensatory ordering factors

sections.title: The counteraction as a system
sections.line: Read as a dynamical system, compensation is why a stuck state cannot simply be fixed from the side that is stuck.

quotes.quote: Because the shadow compensates consciousness, whenever we think we know what the shadow is, its opposite automatically begins to emerge from the unconscious
